notes.summary: Reconstructed all-support raw envelope and actual graded primary-ideal calculus; general normal positivity remains a continuity gap.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves raw C=D suprema for finite continuous obstacles, positivity of usc regularization iff raw continuity, norm Lipschitz, actual integrally closed J_k ideals and increasing factorial formula, and exact homogeneous gauge covariance. These are reconstructed prior facts, not a new general normal envelope theorem.
notes.text:
Let R be excellent local, replaced by its reduction, and a a proper maximal-ideal-primary ideal. Qualified G331 supplies the compact Hausdorff section X_a of ALL centred real semivaluations with v(a)=1. Its independently geometric core uses actual negative effective finite real Cartier presentations on actual primary blowups, with nonnegative degree on every contracted proper integral curve. C is its finite continuous uniform closure, and D its actual decreasing-C-net completion, with bottom allowed. G331 proves their ideal comparison and positive full-fibre descent; it supplies no envelope theorem.

For a finite continuous obstacle phi, define p_C=sup{g in C:g<=phi} and p_D=sup{u in D:u<=phi}. Negative primary constants make these finite and bounded below. If u=inf_i g_i is an admissible D function, the directed open sets {g_i<phi+epsilon} cover X. Compactness selects one index globally, and g_i-epsilon is an admissible C function at least u-epsilon. Therefore p_C=p_D=p. This uses a specified D representation, not membership of an unknown supremum.

The raw p is lower semicontinuous. If p is continuous, the sets {g>p-epsilon} cover X; a finite maximum yields a C function uniformly within epsilon of p. Thus p belongs to C. If p belongs to D, it is also usc, hence continuous. On the exact pointwise semivaluation topology define p*(x)=inf_{U containing x} sup_{y in U}p(y). Continuity of phi gives p<=p*<=min(phi,0). If p* belongs to D, it is an admissible competitor, forcing p*<=p. Consequently p* is geometric iff p is continuous. This equivalence does not prove normal continuity.

The raw operator is monotone and 1-Lipschitz: if phi<=psi+epsilon, every minorant g of phi has g-epsilon<=psi. Interchanging the obstacles proves the norm estimate. Once continuous, p is the actual greatest geometric minorant and is idempotent.

For k>=1 define the ACTUAL ideal J_k(phi)={f in R:v(f)>=-k phi(v) for every v in X}. Addition and multiplication preserve these inequalities. For M>=max(0,-min phi), J_k contains a^ceil(kM), using a^1 when the exponent is zero. If phi is negative somewhere, J_k is proper primary; if phi>=0 everywhere it is the unit ideal. Each J_k is integrally closed: in an ideal-integrality monic equation for f, if v(f)<-k phi(v), the leading term has finite value d v(f), whereas every other term has strictly larger value. A unique finite least term cannot sum to zero. This argument retains nonminimal supports and infinite values. Noetherianity gives finite generation of each individual ideal, not of the graded family.

The relations J_k J_l subset J_(k+l) and J_k^l subset J_(kl) imply that a_k=-v(J_k)/k is an admissible C profile and a_(n!) increases. Its supremum is p. Indeed approximate any g in C below phi by h=-v(I)/s with error less than eta/2. Multiply a large power of I by a power of a to subtract a rational constant between 3eta/2 and 2eta, obtaining g-3eta<=h'<=g-eta. Synchronize its denominator l with a sufficiently large factorial. Its underlying ideal lies in J_l, so h'<=a_l<=a_(n!). Let eta tend to zero. The missing general-normal step is uniform convergence or continuity, not this pointwise formula.

For another primary b, put d(v)=v(b)>0 and H(v)=v/d(v). Both d and 1/d are bounded continuous. Degree-one obstacles and functions transport by phi_b(H(v))=phi_a(v)/d(v). G331's order bijections give p_b(phi_b)(H(v))=p_a(phi_a)(v)/d(v). The defining J_k inequalities are divided by the same d, so the ideals are literally unchanged. Bounded raw regularization also transports because d is positive continuous. Ordinary sectionwise constants without this transport are different obstacles.

Nilpotents are invisible. Dimension-zero local reduction has the unique empty boundary function/envelope. Unit models give zero; unit and zero ideals give no level-one gauge section. Bottom is the least D function. All lower-dimensional normalization centres and all supports remain function and fibre data regardless of ambient top-degree energy.

These are independently reconstructed prior results, not new original completion. Full proofs appear in n1.md, argument.md and the uncompiled P12.3-paper.tex. Rerun: python build_delivery.py; python final_audit.py. Static execution does not verify the mathematics.

notes.summary: New actual decreasing-D-net closure on every excellent reduced germ, with decreasing energy criterion membership proved first.
notes.detailedSummary: Normal zero dichotomy and a strict-majorant insertion construct an actual decreasing C-net for the pointwise infimum of a decreasing D-net. Finite normal centres and full positive conductor descent give all excellent reduced germs. E350 then yields the energy criterion without separately assuming D membership; no arbitrary nondirected infimum or increasing closure is proved.
notes.text:
This is a new closure proof, relative to qualified G331. Let u_i in D decrease and set u=inf_i u_i. First suppose R is an excellent normal local domain with nonempty section. The infimum is usc. If u(x)=0 anywhere, every u_i(x)=0, and G331's normal zero dichotomy makes every u_i identically zero. Thus u=0 belongs to C. Otherwise choose a nonzero term u_i0. The same dichotomy and compact usc imply u_i0<=-c for some finite c>0, including when it is bottom. Therefore u<=-c.

Insertion lemma: for every finite continuous F>u, there exists q in C with u<q<F everywhere. The directed open sets {u_i<F} cover X; select i>=i0 valid globally. Choose an ACTUAL representation g_alpha decreasing to u_i in C. Compact directed open covers select one term g with g<F and g<-c/2 throughout X. Let m=min(F-g)>0 and choose 0<b<1 with b||g||<m/2. Then q=(1-b)g belongs to C, is below F, and exceeds u at finite points by at least bc/2. At bottom points q is finite and also exceeds u. This uses positive scaling, not addition of an inadmissible positive constant.

Let Q consist of all strict C majorants of u. It contains zero. Applying insertion to min(q1,q2), a continuous test which need not be psh, gives a member below both. Thus Q is downward directed. Its infimum is u: for x and finite t>u(x), choose u(x)<l<t and a neighbourhood where u<l. A compact-Hausdorff cutoff interpolates between l near x and a global strict upper bound outside, producing continuous F>u with F(x)<t. When u(x) is bottom, choose any finite l<t. Insertion gives q(x)<t. Reverse pointwise order on Q is an ACTUAL decreasing C-net with infimum u. No nested-net flattening has been assumed.

For finitely many semilocal normal centres apply this argument centrewise and take a finite product of directed sets. For an arbitrary excellent reduced local R, pull the decreasing net back to its finite normalization S, retaining every marked normal centre. The centrewise infima belong to D_S by the preceding construction. Their tuple is constant on every FULL restriction fibre because each pulled-back term is. Qualified G331 positive D descent therefore puts its descent, exactly inf_i u_i, in D_R. This includes conductor-infinite and internal normal fibres. Empty dimension zero is immediate.

Hence D is closed under nonempty decreasing D-nets on EVERY excellent reduced local germ. This also handles nonempty downward-directed families. It proves neither finite-minimum closure nor arbitrary nondirected infimum or increasing closure.

Only after this membership proof apply qualified E350. For a decreasing E1-net, u=inf_i u_i now belongs to D without a separate assumption. Its specified-D energy criterion gives u in E1 iff sup_i F_infinity(u_i^[n]) is finite. On such limits the qualified weak mixed-measure and capacity convergence, test pairing and quasicontinuity apply. Energy has sign E=-F_infinity/n. Nonpure lower-dimensional centres still retain their function/fibre constraints despite zero top-degree contribution.

An obstacle supremum increases. This theorem therefore does not prove general envelope positivity, increasing compactness, variational attainment or Choquet compact-above. notes.summary: Exact BFJ smooth continuous-envelope reconstruction on closed affine algebraically closed characteristic-zero germs only.
notes.detailedSummary: Uses complete immediate published determining-complex envelope proof, substantive closed-face continuity, all retraction infima and the sign-correct uniform ideal estimate. Rational ideal-difference density extends from determining obstacles to every continuous obstacle. No singular or arbitrary-characteristic multiplier/resolution application is made.
notes.text:
The published application is Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson, Valuations and plurisubharmonic singularities, ONLY at a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, dimension at least two. Complete immediate Setting, retraction/projective-limit and Cartier determination units, Definitions 2.1/2.5/2.8 and Proposition 2.7, Proposition 3.11 with proof, and the entire determining-complex envelope argument 3.15–3.22 were read from the exact retained text. Recursive smooth resolution, multiplier subadditivity and historical Izumi/ELS foundations are disclosed published background, not freshly reconstructed in full.

In that setup, Cartier evaluations are determined on a smooth dual complex; rational divisorial points are dense on closed simplices; formal psh functions have the canonical ALL-semivaluation extension g(v)=inf_pi g(r_pi v), and satisfy g<=g composed with r_pi. Proposition 3.11 proves substantive CLOSED-simplex continuity via multiplier estimates; interior convexity alone is insufficient. The nef Weil coefficient cone is weak closed and max-stable.

For a finite continuous h determined on a complex, choose M with -M<=min(h,0). Restrict nef competitors below Z(h) to those above the nef constant divisor -M by finite maximum. Their finite maxima form a directed net with bounded coordinates. Its coefficientwise supremum W is a weak limit in the closed nef cone. Proposition 3.11 and all-retraction extension produce its bounded formal psh function g. This uses BFJ's precise smooth coefficient cone, not a general singular D compactness theorem.

Divisorial coefficient order W<=Z(h) extends to the determining complex by closed-face continuity and dense divisorial points. Thus g(v)<=g(r_pi v)<=h(r_pi v)=h(v) on EVERY support. Any D minorant of h corresponds through qualified G331 to canonical BFJ coefficients below W, so all-retraction order puts it below g. Bottom is separate. Therefore g is the greatest D minorant.

The complete Proposition 3.18 proof gives, for W_j=Z(L^infinity(jW))/j, the estimate W_j<=W<=j/(j+C) W_j, with a constant C depending on the fixed determining complex and envelope. It uses bounded thinness on that complex and actual smooth multiplier subadditivity; it supplies no singular estimate. The zero case uses the unit ideal. Otherwise the section ideals contain completed boundary powers because W>=-M, and their profiles g_j contract exactly to the original local ring by G331. The inequalities extend through all retractions, yielding g_j<=g<=j/(j+C)g_j and g_j>=-M(1+C/j). Consequently 0<=g-g_j<=MC/j uniformly on the FULL compact boundary. Hence g belongs to C.

For arbitrary continuous phi, use G331's dense rational difference span of primary ideal gauges to choose h_l uniformly approaching phi. Principalize the finitely many ideals on a common simple modification in the exact smooth source range; each h_l is determined there. Their positive C envelopes converge uniformly to the raw envelope of phi by n1's Lipschitz bound. Closedness of C proves the continuous-envelope property for every such phi.

Primary gauges follow n1's degree-one transport. A smooth DVR has a singleton boundary and direct envelope min(phi,0); dimension zero is empty. No singular multiplier ideals, arbitrary-characteristic smooth envelopes or arbitrary singular-model cofinality are claimed. The unrelated BFJ3.13 OCR exponent ambiguity is not used; the proof applies the complete legible 3.18 estimate with explicit zero/unit and all-support treatment.

notes.summary: New greatest positive continuous/usc envelopes on normal targets admitting finite dominating domain covers with proved source envelope property.
notes.detailedSummary: A positive full-fibre normalized coefficient trace first constructs a continuous target minorant dominating all target D minorants. Positive finite weights force the source envelope to be fibre constant. An actual decreasing continuous-majorant net handles bounded-above extended usc obstacles and partial bottom. Applies concretely to characteristic-zero normal quadratic cones and smooth factors, not all excellent normal germs.
notes.text:
Let R be an excellent NORMAL local domain, B a finite dominating domain extension, and rho:X_(aB)(B)->X_a(R) restriction, retaining all marked semilocal source centres and all supports. Assume each source centre has the continuous-envelope property. N3 proves this when every marked source centre is a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. This source hypothesis is not assumed for arbitrary excellent normal germs.

Qualified G331 supplies the normalized coefficient trace A:C_B->C_R and A:D_B->D_R. It is positive, a left inverse to pullback, and integrates against a finite probability measure with positive weight at EVERY point of each FULL restriction fibre. Generic inseparable lengths are included. No flatness, Galois action or defectless ramification formula is assumed; B is a dominating domain and no degree is fabricated for vertical components.

For finite continuous phi, let U=P_B(rho*phi) in C_B, using the proved source property and finite product of centres. Put p=A(U). Positivity gives p<=phi. Every target D minorant u pulls back below U, hence u=A(rho*u)<=p. Thus p is an actual greatest geometric minorant, belongs to C_R and is continuous. Its pullback is a source minorant, so rho*p<=U. On each fibre p is a positive weighted average of the finite numbers U(w), and is no greater than any of them. Therefore all values equal the average. We obtain P_R(phi)=A(P_B(rho*phi)) and rho*P_R(phi)=P_B(rho*phi). This proves membership and greatestness before any energy argument.

For extended usc phi:X_R->[-infinity,M], M finite, let F range over finite continuous strict majorants of phi. This family is nonempty and downward directed under minimum. Urysohn cutoff interpolation at each x,t>phi(x) proves inf_F F=phi. The positive envelopes p_F=P_R(F) lie in C and decrease. N2 proves their infimum p belongs to D. Since p_F<=F, p<=phi, and every D minorant of phi is below each p_F. Hence p is the actual greatest envelope, including partial bottom.

Furthermore rho*p=inf_F P_B(rho*F) is an actual decreasing C_B-net limit. It is below rho*phi and dominates every source D minorant of rho*phi, because each such minorant lies below every P_B(rho*F). Thus pullback commutation also holds for the extended envelope; the trace formula follows from the left-inverse property. This avoids the invalid inference that an average of extended bottom values forces fibre constancy.

For bounded obstacles p is bounded and therefore E1. Qualified E350 gives its genuine open-exception quasicontinuity and geometric energy/products. For a general bounded-above extended obstacle, finite energy is equivalent to a uniform bound on the diagonal F_infinity of the decreasing p_F net, by n2 and E350. The sign is E=-F_infinity/n. Exact degree-one primary covariance follows from the class order bijections. No capacity-a.e. replacement of obstacle order, uniqueness of an energy equation or strict concavity is used.

This yields a genuine normal singular sector. For k algebraically closed of characteristic zero and d>=2, take R=k[X,Y,Z,z_3,...,z_d]_m/(XY-Z^2), B=k[s,t,z_3,...,z_d]_n with X=s^2,Y=t^2,Z=st. Both s,t are integral, the extension is finite of field degree two, and the marked fibre has exactly the origin. B satisfies n3. Normality is direct: for M={(i,j) in Z^2:i+j even}, k[s^2,st,t^2]=k[M] intersect k[s,t] in k(s,t). Both larger rings are normal; an element integral over the intersection lies in both. The same intersection identity after adjoining the z variables and localization proves normality of R. Its dimension is d and cotangent dimension d+1, so it is singular. Thus ALL finite continuous obstacles have continuous geometric greatest envelopes on these singular boundaries, and every bounded-above extended usc obstacle has the actual D envelope above, on all supports.

The same transfer applies to any actual finite dominating domain cover satisfying the source property, including appropriate characteristic-zero finite quotient examples. The trace argument itself is characteristic-independent, but the supplied higher-dimensional smooth source theorem is only the exact characteristic-zero range. No assertion that every excellent normal domain admits such a cover is made. Nonnormal targets and arbitrary finite maps are outside this theorem.

notes.summary: New all-characteristic normal singular convergence diagnostic: bounded energy-maximizing primary profiles have a non-D pointwise limit despite capacity convergence.
notes.detailedSummary: On XY=Z^2, I_n=(X^n,XY^(n-1),Y^(2n)) gives u_n increasing from [-2,-1] to -2 at the infinite-X support and -1 elsewhere, hence non-usc. Proves normality, conic reference mass two, capacity error <=2/(1+n epsilon), universal e(I_n)=2n^2+2n and E(u_n)=-1-1/n. Obstacle -1 has positive envelope -1, so this is not a normal-envelope counterexample. Finite diagnostics cover 64 lengths, 48 differences and 272 profile cases only.
notes.text:
For ANY field k and every characteristic let R=k[X,Y,Z]_(X,Y,Z)/(XY-Z^2)=k[s^2,st,t^2]_(s^2,st,t^2), with maximal-ideal gauge. This is excellent, normal and singular. Indeed the nonnegative even-parity exponent semigroup is M intersect the quadrant, where M={(i,j):i+j even}; k[M] is a rank-two Laurent UFD and k[s^2,st,t^2]=k[M] intersect k[s,t]. Intersection of these normal rings is normal in its fraction field, and localization preserves normality. Dimension is two and cotangent dimension three. No resolution or characteristic-dependent invariant-ring theorem is used.

At every boundary point write a=v(X), b=v(Y). The relation gives v(Z)=(a+b)/2 and min(a,b)=1, with extended values. There is a unique point q with a=infinity: it kills (X,Z) and is normalized Y-order on the DVR quotient. Consider the ACTUAL primary ideals I_n=(X^n,XY^(n-1),Y^(2n)) and geometric core profiles u_n=-v(I_n)/n. Their radicals are m. For n=1 the middle generator is literally X, avoiding zero-times-infinity notation. If a<=b then a=1 and u_n=-1. If a>b finite then b=1 and u_n=-min(1+(a-1)/n,2). At q the value is -2. Thus -2<=u_n<=-1, and they increase to h=-1 off q, h(q)=-2.

The monomial semigroup valuations v_L(X)=L, v_L(Y)=1, v_L(Z)=(L+1)/2 converge pointwise to q. In each polynomial, positive s-exponents tend to infinite value and the surviving t-only part has its Y-order; local denominators are units of value zero. This proves convergence on the entire localized ring, including cancellation after combining polynomial coefficients. Since h(v_L)=-1, h is not usc at q and therefore not D. Its usc regularization is -1 in C. The chosen obstacle -1 has actual envelope -1, so this is NOT a normal-envelope counterexample.

The m-blowup has exceptional smooth integral conic XY=Z^2 in projective two-space. The X and Y charts cover this conic and are affine lines even in characteristic two. On the blowup the corresponding charts have coordinates X,Z/X and Y,Z/Y, respectively, up to the base localization. The exceptional generic ring is a DVR with o(X)=o(Y)=o(Z)=1. The tautological restriction is O_conic(1), of degree two. Qualified E350's independently geometric atomic formula therefore gives the reference measure mu(-1)=2 delta_o.

The function z=-v(X) belongs to D via the ACTUAL decreasing primary profiles -v((X)+m^k)=-min(v(X),k). It is nonbottom on this normal branch and has reference moment L_z=2. E350 consequently gives Cap{v(X)>T}<=2/T and Cap{q}=0. For 0<epsilon<1 the exact formulas imply {(-1)-u_n>epsilon}={a>1+n epsilon}, hence capacity at most 2/(1+n epsilon), tending to zero. For epsilon>=1 the strict set is empty. Thus u_n converges in capacity to -1 while its exact pointwise limit is h outside D. Even h is quasicontinuous: the OPEN set {a>T} contains q, has capacity <=2/T, and h is constant on its complement. Boundedness, open-exception quasicontinuity and capacity convergence therefore cannot prove membership of an unknown exact pointwise limit.

The energy is computed universally, not inferred from a finite window. Monomials have exponents in the nonnegative even-parity semigroup. The count below total degree 2k is sum_{d=0}^{k-1}(2d+1)=k^2, so length(R/m^k)=k^2 and e(m)=2. For I_n the exponent generators are A=(2n,0), B=(2,2n-2), C=(0,4n). The bounded complement of their upward convex hull is the polygon 0,A,B,C, area 2n^2+2n; when n=1, B=A.

To justify the multiplicity formula directly, exponents of I_n^k lie in kP, the dilated upward hull. For w in kP intersect M, express w as an orthant remainder plus a convex combination of A,B,C with coefficients summing to k. Round all three down; at most two generators are missing from a k-fold product. A fixed shift (D,D), with D at least three times the largest generator coordinate, supplies that deficit. The shifted point remains in M, and after subtracting a chosen integer sum of k generators the remainder is a nonnegative M exponent. Thus Exp(I_n^k) subset kP intersect M, and (kP intersect M)+(D,D) subset Exp(I_n^k). Pure powers bound the missing exponents in a rectangle of side O(k). The discrepancy from the polygon complement lies in constant-width strips along finitely many edges and has O(k) lattice points. Even-parity lattice density is one-half, with polygon boundary error O(k), as follows by fixed-square tiling. Therefore length(R/I_n^k)=(n^2+n)k^2+O(k), and the Samuel convention gives e(I_n)=2n^2+2n.

Qualified B341/E350 ideal moments and energy give F(u_n,u_n)=2+2/n and E(u_n)=-1-1/n increasing to E(-1)=-1. Every u_n is a bounded E1 minorant of the continuous obstacle -1. Form order gives E(v)<=E(-1) for every E1 minorant of that obstacle. This is consequently an energy-maximizing sequence with a uniformly bounded diagonal size and an infeasible exact increasing pointwise limit. The maximum exists, namely -1. The example refutes the proposed convergence-to-membership inference, not every variational method or the original normal-envelope target. Replacing h by the capacity-equivalent -1 changes its value at q and needs a separate argument in a general problem.

The owned finite_diagnostics.py observed PASS for 64 monomial quotient counts with 1<=n,k<=8, 48 second-difference comparisons, and 272 rational/infinite coordinate profile cases with 1<=n<=16 and 17 explicitly listed pairs. For n=1 lengths are 4,12,24,40,60,84,112,144; for n=2 they are 10,32,66,112,170,240,322,416. Their second differences are 4 and 12. These are exhaustive finite observations only. The universal multiplicity, topology and capacity arguments are above.

notes.summary: Reconstructed sharp full-fibre conductor criterion, all-characteristic nonnormal failure and geometric curve clipping.
notes.detailedSummary: An actual primary conductor mask proves equality on the dense finite-conductor stratum; regularized target positivity is equivalent to continuous fibre-constant source raw envelope. Reconstructs a strictly negative double-plane obstacle with no maximal D minorant. Every excellent reduced-curve geometric envelope is min(phi,0), via actual Cartier/DVR positivity and full descent. No normal residual closure or unrestricted normalization commutation is inferred.
notes.text:
Let S be the finite normalization of an excellent reduced local R, split into ALL local normal centres above the marked point, with full restriction quotient rho and synchronized gauge. Centres are not merely irreducible components. Qualified G331 identifies singleton fibres at finite conductor value and exactly conductor-quotient fibres at infinite value, including internal fibres within one normal centre. Its positive C/D descent is precisely full-fibre constancy. Thus the raw downstairs envelope pulled back is the supremum of upstairs C minorants which are constant on EVERY full fibre; unrestricted normalization commutation is not asserted.

For finite continuous phi, let p_S be the unrestricted upstairs raw envelope. The sharp criterion is: p_R* belongs to D_R iff p_S is continuous and full-fibre constant. Sufficiency follows from n1 and positive C descent. For necessity first prove equality of constrained and unrestricted suprema on the finite-conductor locus. Choose M>0 with -M<=phi, and clip any upstairs C minorant g so -M<=g<=0. Let K_N=c+a^N be the ACTUAL primary ideal, where c is the conductor, and b_N=-(M/N)v(K_N) downstairs. Then -M<=b_N<=0 and b_N=-M on the conductor-infinite stratum. The upstairs function max(g+rho*b_N,-M) is in C, below the obstacle, and constant on all nontrivial fibres, so descends positively. At finite conductor value b_N tends to zero. This proves equality there.

That locus is dense upstairs: the conductor contains a regular element, all centred divisorial valuations have finite value on it, and G331 proves divisorial density on the all-support topology. If p_R* belongs to D, n1 makes p_R continuous. Its continuous pullback u lies below p_S and equals it on the dense locus. Lower semicontinuity of p_S along a net from that locus gives p_S<=u at every point; hence equality and fibre constancy. This criterion contains normal continuity as a CONDITION, not a conclusion. N4 provides it only in its proved finite-cover sector.

The full nonnormal obstruction works over any field. Let R=k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy), S=A times B with A=k[x,z]_(x,z), B=k[y,z]_(y,z). The local ring is their fibre product over k[z]_(z), and clearing unit denominators verifies this identity. The conductor is (x)A times (y)B. The boundary quotient identifies only q_A, killing x with z-order one, and q_B, killing y with z-order one. Their common downstairs support is the nonminimal prime (x,y).

Set phi_A=-1 and phi_B(w)=-1-1/w(y), with reciprocal infinity equal to zero. This is continuous, fibre compatible and strictly negative in [-2,-1]. On B, membership f in m_B^d gives w(f)>=d for every normalized centred w, hence every g in D_B satisfies g(w)<=g(o_B), first for negative ideal profiles, then uniform and actual decreasing limits. Since phi_B(o_B)=-2, every B minorant is <=-2 everywhere; the constant -2 is admissible. Thus the unrestricted source envelope is (-1,-2), continuous but incompatible at the identified fibre.

For n>=1 take the actual A-primary ideals J_n=(x^n,xz^(n-1),z^(2n)), paired with constant -2 on B. Their profiles agree at q_A,q_B and descend positively to C_R. With a=w(x),b=w(z), min(a,b)=1, the A value is -1 if a<=b, is -min(1+(a-1)/n,2) if a>b finite, and is -2 at q_A. The literal n=1 generator avoids zero-times-infinity. These minorants increase and prove the exact raw downstairs envelope: -1 on A off q_A, -2 at q and everywhere on B. The B order bound gives the matching universal upper bound. Monomial x-weight tending to infinity approaches q_A, so the raw envelope is not usc. N1 rules out geometric usc regularization. There is no maximal D minorant: a maximal minorant would dominate every competitor by finite maxima and equal the non-usc supremum. This is a nonnormal obstruction and unrestricted normalization commutation failure, not a normal residual counterexample or full P12.6 theorem.

For every excellent reduced curve the geometric comparison is complete. Its finite link is the set of local DVR normalization centres q, with v_q=ord_q/a_q and a_q=ord_q(a)>0. The conductor has finite value at every point, so all restriction fibres are singletons. On a DVR the actual closed-point Cartier divisor and its nonnegative real multiples give all finite nonpositive constants; unit gives zero. Finite products and qualified positive C descent give every finite nonpositive branch vector downstairs. Decreasing cuts give all extended nonpositive vectors in D. Hence the actual geometric greatest envelope on this finite link is P_geom phi(q)=min(phi(q),0)=P_ideal phi(q), including mixed zero and partial bottom. Primary gauge changes are the exact positive branch order ratios. Qualified E350 gives reference measure sum_q f_q a_q delta_vq with actual residue degrees and finite-energy class the finite vectors.

This valuative boundary cone is distinct from literal classical/CLD logarithmic radial extension. A complex nodal mixed-zero slope can violate the common-node usc/closed-disc maximum principle although its boundary vector (-1,0) is geometric here. No general CLD theorem is used as a premise.
